sentences.text: 1  (By Sri. A.Vijay Kumar, Adv.)
JUDGMENT
This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 29-07-2023 at about 5.00 p.m., the Petitioner was riding Ola Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EV-0078 towards her home, BHCS Layout, 3rd Main and 7th Cross Junction,
Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NE-8648 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the scooter and accident occurred.
Due to the accident, Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
She was immediately taken to BGS Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she was treated as an inpatient.
Due to the accidental injuries, she is suffering from permanent disability and is unable to lead normal life as earlier.

It is claimed that the Petitioner has spent huge amount for treatment,
medicines, conveyance and other charges.

At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 57 years,
working as a Lecturer in Kumaran's PU College, Padmanabhanagar, Bengaluru and drawing salary of Rs.73,651/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries, she has lost her earning capacity and income.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1- Insurer and Respondent No.2-Insured.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.

4. The respondent no.1 has filed its written statement and admitted the issuance of policy to the alleged offending vehicle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
Further, denied the contents of petition averments in toto.

It has denied that the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, the accident has occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the rider (petitioner) of scooter.
It has contended that the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties as the owner and insurer of scooter were not arrayed as respondents in the petition.
Further, it has contended that the petitioner was not wearing helmet and not holding DL at the time of accident.
Further, the driver of offending vehicle was not having valid DL as on the date of accident.

It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by her, expenses incurred by her and disability suffered by her.
Further contended that the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant, excessive and unreasonable.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. The respondent no.2 has denied all the averments of the petition inter-alia contending that the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, the accident has occurred due to negligent riding of scooter by the petitioner.
The offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.1 and policy was valid as on the date of accident and the driver was holding valid DL and has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

sentences.text:
On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that she sustained injuries when she was going in Ola Scooter bearing No.KA-41-EV-0078 on 29-07-2023 about 5.00 p.m. near BHCS Layout, 3rd Main road, 7th Cross Jucntion, Bengaluru District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-NE-8648?
2. What compensation Petitioner is entitled ?
3. What order ?

7. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.15.
8.
Respondents have not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.

9. By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10.
ISSUE NO.1:-

The case of the petitioner is that on 29-07-2023 at about 5.00 p.m., the she was riding Ola Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EV-0078 towards her home, BHCS Layout, 3rd Main and 7th Cross Junction, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NE-8648 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the scooter and accident occurred.
Due to the accident, Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

11. In order to substantiate her case, petitioner has examined as PW-1 and got marked the police documents at Ex.P.1 to 10 i.e., FIR, complaint, sketch, mahazar, notice, reply, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.
As per wound certificate petitioner has sustained grievous injuries over right foot and over left thumb and palm, right palm, right ankle TEL sprain + incomplete lateral malleolar fracture.

12. The respondent No.1 has contended that the petitioner was riding her vehicle with out following the traffic rules and regulation and the alleged accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle.
He has also taken contention that at time of accident petitioner was not wearing helmet and was not having effective driving licence.
13. Keeping in view of the arguments addressed by the learned counsel for the respondent once again I have perused the material available on record.

However on perusal of the charge sheet,
Padmaja B S vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43889468/
3 complaint and FIR, prima-facie establish that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and not on the part of petitioner.

sentences.text: Neither the respondent has challenged the charge sheet before any authority nor rebut the evidence lead by the petitioner.
14. On perusal of police and medical records, it appears that the petitioner sustained injuries in a RTA.
The police records show that due to rash and negligent act of the offending vehicle the accident was caused.
As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
There is no materials to disbelieve or rebut the evidence of the petitioner and charge sheet has been filed against the offending vehicle.
Therefore, this tribunal concludes that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Thereby the accident occurred and petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2 :- As discussed in issue No.1 that it was the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
So far as quantum of compensation is concerned the Petitioner has stated that she has spent more than 50,000/- towards treatment, medical, food and conveyance and other incidental expenses.

It is found that the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries over right foot and over left thumb and palm, right palm, right ankle TEL sprain + incomplete lateral malleolar fracture as per Ex.P.9-wound certificate and doctor opined that the petitioner has sustained simple as well as grievous injury in the RTA.
She has stated that she has spent Rs.50,000/- towards medical expenses and was working as a Lecturer in Kumaran's PU college and drawing salary of Rs.73,651/-p.m.
In support her avocation, income she has produced Ex.P.15- pay slip.
It is pertinent to note that it is not proved that due to the accidental injuries she is suffering from difficulties and is unable to work as earlier.
She has not examined the doctor to prove the permanent disability suffered by her.
Absolutely there is no disability stated and there is no evidence that the injuries has affected her day to day activities.
She has not produced the discharge summary to show that she taken treatment as an inpatient.
She has produced medical bills at Ex.P.12 amounting to Rs.10,877/-.

Considering the nature of injury, treatment taken by Petitioner, her age and the date of accident, I deem it proper to award 50,000/- of global compensation under all the conventional heads, as the Petitioner has suffered some sort of pain and had to take treatment for his injuries.
16. Liability: Respondent No.1 being the insurer and the Respondent No.2 being the insured of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.

However,
Respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
17. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos.1 &
2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.50,000/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.1 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount, entire amount with interest Padmaja B S vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43889468/
4 shall be disbursed to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
